title: Seeded Random Suite
description: PROGRAM: Seeded Random Suite (['seed generator', 'coin flip']). Deterministic randomness lab: the boundless PRNG drives coin flips reproducibly. This record IS the complete runnable program — copy it to a file and run with python3.
demo:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SIGNATURE MIX: seed PRNG + coin flips -> reproducible random lab."""
def prng(seed):
    a = seed & 0xFFFFFFFF
    def nxt():
        nonlocal a
        a = (a + 0x6D2B79F5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        t = a
        t = ((t ^ (t >> 15)) * (t | 1)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        t ^= (t + ((t ^ (t >> 7)) * (t | 61))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        return ((t ^ (t >> 14)) & 0xFFFFFFFF) / 4294967296
    return nxt

def experiment(seed, n=1000):
    r = prng(seed)
    heads = sum(1 for _ in range(n) if r() < 0.5)
    return heads

if __name__ == "__main__":
    h1, h2 = experiment(7), experiment(7)
    h3 = experiment(8)
    print("seed 7: %d/1000 heads (twice: %d)" % (h1, h2))
    assert h1 == h2 and h1 != h3 and 400 < h1 < 600
    print("OK: seeded experiments reproduce exactly")

description: PROGRAM: Word Game Arcade (['hangman', 'word scrambler']). Word-game arcade: unscramble challenge plus scripted hangman. This record IS the complete runnable program — copy it to a file and run with python3.
demo:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SIGNATURE MIX: hangman + scrambler -> word game arcade."""
import random
def scramble(w, seed):
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    if len(w)<=3: return w
    m=list(w[1:-1]); rng.shuffle(m)
    return w[0]+"".join(m)+w[-1]
def hangman_won(word, guesses):
    found=set()
    for g in guesses:
        if g in word: found.add(g)
        if set(word)<=found: return True
    return set(word)<=found

if __name__ == "__main__":
    target="archive"
    scr=scramble(target,5)
    print("unscramble:",scr)
    assert sorted(scr)==sorted(target) and scr[0]==target[0]
    assert hangman_won("data",["d","a","t","x"])
    assert not hangman_won("quiz",["a","e","i"])
    print("OK: scramble + hangman both playable")

description: PROGRAM: Signal Banners (['morse code', 'banner maker']). Renders Morse code as big ASCII banners — signals you can read across the room. This record IS the complete runnable program — copy it to a file and run with python3.
demo:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SIGNATURE MIX: morse + banner -> signal banners."""
DOT=["  #  ","  #  ","     ","     ","     "]
DASH=[" ##### "," ##### ","       ","       ","       "]
GAP=["  "]*5
def morse_banner(code):
    rows=[""]*5
    for sym in code:
        g=DOT if sym=="." else DASH if sym=="-" else GAP
        for i in range(5): rows[i]+=g[i]
    return "\n".join(rows)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    out=morse_banner("...")   # S
    print(out)
    assert out.count("#")==6
    out2=morse_banner(".-")   # A
    assert out2.count("#")==12
    print("OK: morse banners rendered")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SIGNATURE MIX: pig latin + scrambler -> wordplay lab."""
import random, re
VOW=set("aeiou")
def pig(w):
    w=w.lower(); i=0
    while i<len(w) and w[i] not in VOW: i+=1
    return (w if i==0 else w[i:]+w[:i])+("way" if i==0 else "ay")
def scramble(w,seed=2):
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    if len(w)<=3: return w
    m=list(w[1:-1]); rng.shuffle(m)
    return w[0]+"".join(m)+w[-1]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    w="archive"
    print("pig:",pig(w),"| scrambled:",scramble(w))
    assert pig("archive")=="archiveway"
    s=scramble("testing")
    assert s[0]=="t" and s[-1]=="g" and sorted(s)==sorted("testing")
    print("OK: wordplay lab transforms verified")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SIGNATURE MIX: coin flip + countdown -> decision timer."""
import random
def decide(options,seed=4):
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    return options[int(rng.random()*len(options))]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    choice=decide(["ship it","sleep on it","ask Manon"])
    print("the coin says:",choice)
    for i in range(3,0,-1): print(i)
    print("DECIDED:",choice)
    assert choice in ("ship it","sleep on it","ask Manon")
    assert decide(["a","b"],seed=4)==decide(["a","b"],seed=4)
    print("OK: decision timer is deterministic")
